claims: Hormozi posts ~29 pieces of content a day, then re-uses the hooks that perform until they stop working
System loops: Claude generates hook -> small model scores it against your winners/losers -> keep only hooks scoring >90%
Creator tested for a few months with 'a couple different Jev-adjacent models'; his own hand-written hooks beat AI-written hooks 'every single time' in A/B posting
Now he writes hooks himself and only uses the system to score them -- that worked much better; 'don't outsource your creativity to an AI agent'

Screen: Jev scored 16 hooks against the last 5 months of TikTok openers; three cleared the bar: 'AI engineers are looting Alex Hormozi' 91%, 'Anybody can reverse engineer Hormozi's virality' 88%, 'Anybody can reverse engineer Hormozi's success' 82%
how_to_steps: Scrape your own past videos (TikTok via Apify) and save hooks with view counts into hooks.json, split into winners and flops around median views
Have the main model (Claude) brainstorm many candidate hooks
Feed each candidate plus the winners/losers file to a small, fast model (Jev) and ask it to predict whether the hook will perform; get a score
Loop until you have enough hooks above ~90%; kill the rest
Creator's revised version: write hooks yourself 'off the dome', then use the scorer only to rank them; post multiple versions and let real views decide
on_screen_only: Title card: 'The failed content kryptonite' with Hormozi photo
Pipeline diagram: your TikTok -> Apify -> hooks.json; Claude (writes hooks) -> new hook -> Jev (scores each hook) -> score -> top hooks; loop diagram Claude <-> Jev with 'kill' branch

relevance.why: Directly applicable to marketing our apps on short-form: a tiny, cheap loop (scrape own hooks -> score new ones) with a sober finding that AI-written hooks underperform human ones. Honest negative result is more valuable than the hype pieces.

implement_score.why: Cheap: one Apify TikTok actor run (or manual export) to build hooks.json, then a Claude Code skill that scores our hand-written hooks against winners/flops using a cheap small model (Haiku, or Jev if it is real). Half a day. Use it as a scorer/ranker, not a writer, per the creator's own test.
